correctness.rationale: An invariant matching for a six-cycle can only pair opposite roots, so the kernel is defined over k (not pointwise rational). The base-point-free pencil of the three quadratic divisors has degree two and is separable in odd characteristic; its deck transformation pairs the roots, is determined on three of them, and descends because Frobenius permutes the pairs. Conversely, a projective involution commuting with the six-cycle acts as its displacement by three. The Richelot pencil criterion gives geometric decomposition exactly on this locus. For the polarized descent, use the product of the pushforwards to the two degree-two elliptic quotients by the lifted involution and its product with the hyperelliptic involution. The two self-composites with pullbacks are [2] and the cross-composites vanish by the opposite involution actions. The resulting degree-four map has pullback twice the principal polarization and kills the classes from each paired Weierstrass divisor, so its kernel is exactly the canonical Richelot kernel. A rational change of coordinate may change the scalar on the sextic but not these lift tests. In split coordinates both lifts (and maps) are defined over k. In nonsplit coordinates x↦d/x, the lifts use opposite square roots of d³; Frobenius swaps the quotient maps, giving the polarized quadratic Weil restriction, not an isomorphism of the source Jacobian. The degree-three parameter test gives (q³−q)/6 per involution in each case (nonsquares in the cubic field for the split case, nonsquare discriminants of x²−tx+d for the nonsplit case). Centralizer orders supply the two stated counts without multiplicity. Over odd extensions the nonsplit identity x⁶f(d/x)=d³ f(x) pairs opposite nonzero character contributions. The contribution at 0 is −1 and there are two points at infinity, giving Q+1; in particular the odd coefficients of the Weil numerator vanish by the trace and reciprocity. A new exact enumeration inspected all p⁶ monic coefficient vectors for p=3 and 5 by irreducibility and binary-form invariance; it found 116 and 2580 irreducibles, with nonsplit counts 12 and 200. Independent F_(p²) character sums yielded the claimed b histograms, using b=(N₂−p²−1)/2. No frozen scripts were executed.
residual_risks: The finite census establishes only q=3 and 5. The general result does not follow from enumeration, and there is no converse from odd trace balance to this type of Richelot kernel.

value.rationale: This concerns a canonical quotient selected by an irreducible branch divisor, not an arbitrary slice of coefficients. The arithmetic type tells whether the geometric elliptic factors are individually defined over the base and predicts vanishing odd traces on one stratum. The q=3 and q=5 tables are complete marked-model spectra at the first two odd field sizes and distinguish a single spectral class from four with differing masses; the weights are meaningful for sampling monic models and are not supplied by an unweighted list of possible Weil polynomials. Their use is deliberately finite.
residual_risks: No claim for spectral weights in larger fields, nor identification of the original Jacobian with its Richelot codomain.
